description: The generic steel-framed sidewalk vending cart -- bare counter, twin gas burner and a striped awning on corner posts, with condiment bags hung from the frame.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Steel-framed sidewalk vending cart on castors with a bare stainless counter, twin ring gas burner set into one end, four corner posts carrying a flat striped fabric awning above, plastic bags of chillies and cut limes hung from the frame rail, gas cylinder and stacked bowls on the lower shelf Materials: Dented stainless counter with grease film, soot around the burner rings, sun-bleached striped awning fabric with frayed edges, cloudy stretched plastic bags, rust at the frame welds.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 1,216/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases. Open frame: turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Ten-band proxy comparison 0.018 width of H against 0.170 for the first build; envelope 1.40 x 2.017 x 1.003 m (v4: the awning widened 60 mm each side past the frame on the owner's review and the width re-declared 1.28 -> 1.40).
featureReviews.notes: THE WIDTH WAS A DECLARED ASPECT RATIO and the band table said so in a way no plate could: a near-CONSTANT +0.17 of H in every one of the ten bands while the depth was out by 0.03. A uniform offset in every band is an aspect, not a shape -- the same signature the roti griddle stand showed in this session. The proxy then gave a second finding for free: it reads 0.59 H at the frame bands and 0.596 H at the awning bands, so THE AWNING IS AS WIDE AS THE FRAME and does not overhang sideways, where this build ran the cloth 0.10 m proud of a frame already 0.32 m too wide. Bands 8-9 depth are NOT evidence and were not chased: reference depth 0.493 H at band 8 under 0.405 H at band 9 is a solid WEDGE, which is Meshy thickening thin cloth. v4 (owner review) overrides the as-wide-as-the-frame reading: the cloth now overhangs the posts by 80 mm each side so more of the perimeter is covered.

featureReviews.evidence: Six-band cream/red stripe canvas across two sloped panels with valances; grime multiply.
Four translucent bags with chilli and lime blocks on the rail, twin burner with rings, gas bottle and three bowl stacks on the shelf, rust collars at eight joints.

name: Street Stall Canopy Cart
nameTh: รถเข็นกางเต็นท์
notes: Deliberately the generic and undressed vendor cart of the kit: a bare counter, a burner and an awning, with no dish-specific equipment on it. That is what makes it the piece a level builder places in rows and dresses differently each time, which is worth more than another single-dish cart. It is distinct from the papaya salad cart, which is glass-fronted with a mortar and a folded tarp, and from the noodle soup cart, which is enclosed around a stainless broth well. The awning on four corner posts is what carries the silhouette at distance. No destruction groups: it is a static vendor prop, not a breakable. Declared size corrected 1.80 x 2.10 x 0.90 -> 1.28 x 2.10 x 1.00 at model time (2026-09-01). The ten-band proxy comparison read the first build a near-CONSTANT +0.17 of H too wide in every one of the ten bands while the depth was out by only 0.03 -- a uniform offset across every band is an aspect ratio rather than a shape, the same signature the roti griddle stand showed in the same session. The proxy wants 0.59 H = 1.24 m at the frame bands and 0.596 H = 1.25 m at the awning bands, which is the second finding: THE AWNING IS AS WIDE AS THE FRAME and does not overhang sideways at all, where the build ran the cloth 0.10 m proud of a frame that was already 0.32 m too wide. Depth grew to 1.00 because the awning is the deep part (0.49 H) over a 0.65 m frame. Rebuilt residual 0.018 width.
